Package hadur2.core.physics

Class SimpleAims

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.physics.SimpleAims
public final class SimpleAims extends Object
DODGE-1: where the simple guns would have aimed a wave's bullet at us, as Saguaro's ShotDodger reads them (docs/bench/rivals-source-read.md): head-on, linear, circular and averaged linear predicted tick by tick, and the two one-line linear aims small robots use (bearing plus lateral velocity over bullet speed, and its arcsine), each aimed on the wave's tick or one or two ticks before it (the enemy reads our scan a tick late, and its gun turns a tick after it aims), from where the enemy stood on that tick at where we stood. The predicted paths stop at the walls, where a robot's centre stays 18 px in.

An aim is indexed lag * TYPES + type. Two entries a lag are not angles but what ShotDodger builds more aims from: our lateral velocity seen from the enemy (LATERAL, for a linear aim with its own divisor) and the enemy's body turn on the tick after the lag's (TURN_AFTER, for a gun that turns with the body). A state is {x, y, heading, velocity, turn, averageVelocity, enemyX, enemyY, enemyHeading}: ours, then the enemy's, in px, radians on Robocode's compass, px/tick and radians per tick. Pure: no engine types, no clock, no randomness.
